For a known user u assigned to group g(u), use the same graph G₋g(u), built without that group’s training transitions, during training and inference. Persist group assignments and exclude every transition from each group member, including contributions to graph normalization and auxiliary statistics. This preserves training-time exclusion and graph size; it does not eliminate all possible distribution shift. This recommendation follows the cross-fitting principle: training features must exclude their own supervisory contributions. [Scikit-learn’s cross-fitting documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/preprocessing/plot_target_encoder_cross_val.html) and [CatBoost’s analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09516) explain the underlying leakage and prediction-shift problem; applying it to user-transition graphs is a methodological inference.

Averaging all K exclusion graphs restores self-support: u’s transitions appear in K−1 graphs. For raw additive counts, their average equals (K−1)/K times the full graph, so row normalization can recover the full-graph transition probabilities exactly. Averaging nonlinear features or prediction scores lacks that identity but still admits self-support through those K−1 branches. It also changes inference features from one excluded-group graph to an ensemble containing the user’s contributions. Standard target encoding permits full-training mappings for genuinely unseen observations, but a known user is not unseen at the grouping unit. Historical self-support alone is not held-out-label leakage; direct target-encoding leakage occurs when a training target transition contributes to its own feature. [TargetEncoder documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing.TargetEncoder.html).

For ensemble inference that preserves exclusion, use repeated user partitions and average only the branch excluding u’s group in each partition, with matching training-time feature construction. Build every graph exclusively from permitted training histories; exclude validation and test targets throughout.
